tests.title: NewRun returns a fully initialised Run with all required fields populated
given: a temporary git repository created via gitx.New(t.TempDir(), nil) with an initial commit
a lang.Detection with a primary profile
tests.when: engine.NewRun is called with the repo root, git handle, options and detection
then: the returned error is nil
run.Root equals the symlink-resolved root
run.Git is the provided git handle
run.Lang is the provided detection
run.Ledger is non-nil
run.Gate is non-nil
tests.pseudocode: dir := t.TempDir(); g := gitx.New(dir, nil); initRepo(g); det := lang.Detection{...}; run, err := engine.NewRun(dir, g, opts, det); assert err == nil; assert run.Root != ""; assert run.Ledger != nil; assert run.Gate != nil; assert run.Git == g; assert run.Lang == det

tests.title: NewRun returns a nil Run and non-nil error when the root is not a git repository
given: a temporary directory that is not a git repository
tests.when: engine.NewRun is called with that directory as root
then: the returned Run is nil
the returned error is non-nil and describes the problem
tests.pseudocode: dir := t.TempDir(); run, err := engine.NewRun(dir, gitx.New(dir, nil), opts, det); assert run == nil; assert err != nil; assert strings.Contains(err.Error(), "git") || strings.Contains(err.Error(), "repository")

tests.title: Ledger.Snapshot records untracked files as a map; on git error the snapshot is nil
given: a temporary git repository with an initial commit
two untracked files created in the tree
tests.when: Ledger.Snapshot is called
then: the snapshot contains both untracked files
calling Snapshot on a repo where UntrackedFiles would error results in a nil snapshot (meaning commit everything)
tests.pseudocode: g := initRepo(t.TempDir()); writeFile("a.txt"); writeFile("b.txt"); ledger := engine.NewLedger(); ledger.Snapshot(ctx, g); assert ledger.snapshot["a.txt"] == true; assert ledger.snapshot["b.txt"] == true; // error case: ledger2 with broken git; ledger2.Snapshot(ctx, brokenGit); assert ledger2.snapshot == nil

tests.title: Ledger.Changes classifies paths as test, docs, implementation, gate-config, scratch or protected
given: a temporary git repository with an initial commit
files created: foo_test.go, README.md, main.go, Makefile, .agent-fox/scratch/tmp.txt, and a protected file spec.json
Ledger.SetOwned called with .agent-fox/scratch/
Ledger.SetProtected called with spec.json
tests.when: Ledger.Changes is called with the git handle and the initial commit as since-ref
then: foo_test.go is classified as Kind=test
README.md is classified as Kind=docs
main.go is classified as Kind=implementation
Makefile is classified as Kind=gate-config
.agent-fox/scratch/tmp.txt is classified as Kind=scratch
spec.json is classified as Kind=protected
tests.pseudocode: changes, err := ledger.Changes(ctx, g, initialCommit); assert err == nil; byPath := map changes by Path; assert byPath["foo_test.go"].Kind == "test"; assert byPath["README.md"].Kind == "docs"; assert byPath["main.go"].Kind == "implementation"; assert byPath["Makefile"].Kind == "gate-config"

tests.title: Ledger.Commit leaves snapshot files in the tree and warns about left-alone and unlisted files
given: a temporary git repository with an initial commit
two untracked files pre.txt and new.txt exist before Snapshot
Ledger.Snapshot is called (records pre.txt and new.txt)
a phase creates another file phase.txt and modifies a tracked file
tests.when: Ledger.Commit is called with a message, noVerify=false, and reported changes that do not include phase.txt
then: the commit succeeds and returns a non-empty commit hash
pre.txt and new.txt are still untracked (not in the commit)
a WarnUntrackedFilesLeftAlone warning is emitted for pre.txt and new.txt
a WarnUnlistedFileCommitted warning is emitted for phase.txt
tests.pseudocode: ledger.Snapshot(ctx, g); writeFile("phase.txt"); modifyTracked("tracked.go"); hash, err := ledger.Commit(ctx, g, "msg", false, []FileChange{{Path: "tracked.go"}}); assert err == nil; assert hash != ""; assert fileExists("pre.txt"); warnings := recorder.Warnings(); assert containsCode(warnings, WarnUntrackedFilesLeftAlone); assert containsCode(warnings, WarnUnlistedFileCommitted)

tests.title: Ledger.SetOwned marks paths as run-owned and SetProtected classifies changed protected paths
given: a temporary git repository with an initial commit
a file .agent-fox/scratch/notes.txt created
a file spec/tasks.json modified
tests.when: Ledger.SetOwned is called with .agent-fox/scratch/ and Ledger.SetProtected is called with spec/tasks.json, then Ledger.Changes is called
then: the scratch file is classified as Kind=scratch
spec/tasks.json is classified as Kind=protected
tests.pseudocode: ledger.SetOwned(".agent-fox/scratch/"); ledger.SetProtected("spec/tasks.json"); changes, _ := ledger.Changes(ctx, g, base); scratch := findChange(changes, ".agent-fox/scratch/notes.txt"); assert scratch.Kind == "scratch"; prot := findChange(changes, "spec/tasks.json"); assert prot.Kind == "protected"

tests.title: Ledger.SetForeignPath causes matching untracked files to be left alone during Commit
given: a temporary git repository with an initial commit
Ledger.Snapshot called (empty snapshot)
an untracked file .specs/other_spec/prd.md created after snapshot
Ledger.SetForeignPath called with a predicate matching .specs/other_spec/*

a WarnUntrackedFilesLeftAlone warning is emitted for it
tests.pseudocode: ledger.SetForeignPath(func(p string) bool { return strings.HasPrefix(p, ".specs/other_spec/") }); writeFile(".specs/other_spec/prd.md"); writeFile("real_change.go"); hash, err := ledger.Commit(ctx, g, "msg", false, nil); assert err == nil; assert fileStillUntracked(".specs/other_spec/prd.md")

tests.title: Ledger.OwnChange returns true when the tree has changes not in the snapshot, false otherwise

then: OwnChange returns false when only pre.txt exists (it is in the snapshot)
OwnChange returns true after own.txt is created (it is not in the snapshot)
tests.pseudocode: writeFile("pre.txt"); ledger.Snapshot(ctx, g); assert ledger.OwnChange(ctx, g) == false; writeFile("own.txt"); assert ledger.OwnChange(ctx, g) == true

tests.title: Ledger.FlagGateEdits warns about gate-config edits, deleted tests, rewritten golden files and added skip markers

tests.title: GateCache.Run returns a cached result on a cache hit and records cached: true in timings
given: a temporary git repository with an initial commit
a GateCache with a pre-populated entry for (treeHash, 'make test')
tests.when: GateCache.Run is called with the same tree hash and command
then: the returned checks.Result matches the cached entry
no subprocess is executed
a timing entry is recorded with cached: true
tests.pseudocode: cache := engine.NewGateCache(); cachedResult := checks.Result{OK: true, Command: "make test"}; cache.Store(treeHash, "make test", cachedResult); result := cache.Run(ctx, runner, root, "make test", timeout, "baseline"); assert result == cachedResult; assert recorder.LastTiming().Cached == true

tests.title: GateCache.Run calls checks.Run on a cache miss, stores the result, and returns it
given: a temporary git repository with an initial commit
an empty GateCache
a runner that returns a known checks.Result
tests.when: GateCache.Run is called with a command
then: checks.Run is invoked
the result is stored in the cache
a second call with the same tree hash returns the cached result without invoking checks.Run again
tests.pseudocode: cache := engine.NewGateCache(); callCount := 0; runner := func(...) { callCount++; return ... }; r1 := cache.Run(ctx, runner, root, "make test", timeout, "label"); assert callCount == 1; r2 := cache.Run(ctx, runner, root, "make test", timeout, "label"); assert callCount == 1; assert r1 == r2

tests.title: GateCache computes tree hash via rev-parse HEAD^{tree} when clean and write-tree when dirty
given: a temporary git repository with an initial commit (clean tree)
the HEAD tree hash is known
tests.when: the tree hash is computed on a clean tree and then on a dirty tree (after modifying a file without committing)
then: on a clean tree the hash equals git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}
on a dirty tree the hash differs from the clean-tree hash
tests.pseudocode: cleanHash := cache.treeHash(ctx, g); expected, _ := g.RevParse(ctx, "HEAD^{tree}"); assert cleanHash == expected; writeFile("dirty.go"); dirtyHash := cache.treeHash(ctx, g); assert dirtyHash != cleanHash

tests.title: GateCache.RunGate runs multiple commands through the cache and returns a GateResult

then: the returned GateResult has two Checks entries

tests.pseudocode: gr := cache.RunGate(ctx, runner, root, []string{"make lint", "make test"}, timeout, "baseline"); assert len(gr.Checks) == 2; assert gr.Ran() == true; assert gr.OK() == true

tests.title: GateResult type is exported from engine with Ran, OK, couldNotRun, aborted and failing methods, and compareGate and landable are exported
given: a GateResult with mixed check results: one OK, one failed, one aborted
tests.when: the GateResult methods and compareGate/landable are called
then: Ran() returns true
OK() returns false (not all passed)
couldNotRun() returns false (no exit -1 or timeout)
aborted() returns true (one check was aborted)
failing() returns the failed check
compareGate returns the worst verdict
landable returns false for a regressed verdict
tests.pseudocode: gr := engine.GateResult{Checks: []checks.Result{{OK: true}, {OK: false, ExitCode: 1}, {Aborted: true}}}; assert gr.Ran(); assert !gr.OK(); _, cnr := gr.CouldNotRun(); assert !cnr; assert gr.Aborted(); assert len(gr.Failing()) == 1; v := engine.CompareGate(baseline, gr); assert !engine.Landable(v, false)

tests.title: Park commits with noVerify=true under a cancellation-proof context and returns the checkout to the base branch
